Notes:
   Marjorie Wallace, the 1973 winner, became the first titleholder not to complete her reign, when in March 1974, she was fired for "failing to fulfill the basic requirements of the job". Organisers extended an offer to first runner-up Evangeline Pascual of the Philippines to complete the duties of Miss World for the remainder of the year, but without holding the title; when Pascual turned down that offer, organisers next turned to second runner-up Patsy Yuen of Jamaica, who accepted.(
   The 2002 pageant was originally to be held in Abuja, Nigeria, but was relocated to the United Kingdom after anti-pageant rioting.
   The 2008 pageant was originally to be held in Kyiv, Ukraine, but was relocated to South Africa after a diplomatic crisis between Russia and Georgia.
   Three countries have achieved back-to-back wins: Sweden in 1951 and 1952, United Kingdom in 1964 and 1965, and India in 1999 and 2000.

WWD remembers all the winners in the beauty pageant history.
Miss USA 2024 Alma Cooper and Miss USA 1952 Jackie Loughery, miss usa winners list
Miss Utah USA 2023 Noelia Voigt crowned Miss USA 2023
Miss Utah USA 2023 Noelia Voigt crowned Miss USA 2023
Miss New Mexico USA 2023 Bianca Wright
Miss Maryland USA 2023 Savena Mushinge
The 73rd Miss USA pageant crowned Alma Cooper of Michigan as Miss USA 2024 on Sunday in Los Angeles. She received the crown from Miss USA 2023 Savannah Gankiewicz, who took over the title after former Miss USA 2023 Noelia Voigt resigned in May.
Cooper was the first active-duty Army officer to compete in the Miss Michigan USA competition. She had previously competed in Miss Michigan Teen USA, placing first runner-up in 2017 and as a semi-finalist in 2018 and 2019.
Alma Cooper, Miss Michigan USA at the 73rd annual Miss USA Pageant at Peacock Theater on August 4, 2024 in Los Angeles, California.
Cooper will go on to represent the United States at the Miss Universe 2024 pageant in Mexico in November.
Created by the Miss Universe Organization, which was founded by Catalina Swimwear, the first Miss USA pageant was held on June 28, 1952, in Long Beach, Calif. The pageant was initially organized as a way to promote Catalina Swimwear, and the winner of the pageant was awarded a contract to represent the company. The competition includes evaluations by a panel of judges who award scores to delegates based on their presentations of eveningwear, swimwear, as well as their responses to questions that spanned social and cultural topics.
While it does remain a beauty pageant, the organization’s current messaging promotes Miss USA winners as ambassadors of women’s empowerment and philanthropy.
Who owns the Miss USA?
Among its owners, the Miss USA pageant was under Donald Trump’s helm from 1996 to 2015 until talent management company IMG purchased it (along with Miss Universe and Miss Teen USA). In October 2022, Thai transgender entrepreneur Anne Jakrajutatip acquired the Miss Universe Organization.
Laylah Rose, a fashion designer and the founder of Laylah Rose Couture, took over Miss USA and Miss Teen USA in 2023.
(Original Caption) Proudly showing their trophies are the winners in Wednesday night's judging of the "Miss U.S.A." division of the "Miss Universe" contest. Left to right: Miss New York City, Rene Roy, Fourth Place; Miss New York, Karen Huitman, third place; Miss South Carolina, Mirian Stevenson, "Miss U.S.A."; Miss Virginia, Ellen Whitehead, second place; and Miss Texas, Betty Lee, fifth place. The South Carolina belle last night won the "Miss Universe" crown to win the third annual beauty pageant at Long Beach.
American Miss Universe winners
Miss USA 1954 Miriam Stevenson is remembered as the first American to win the Miss Universe title and the only one who received a tied final score — she disputed the crown with Martha Rocha of Brazil. Both faced a last decisive round in the competition, and Stevenson ended up securing the title due to having a “better physique” for what Catalina Swimwear was looking for.
Since Stevenson, eight Miss USA winners have gone on to become Miss Universe, including:  
• Miss Universe 1956 Carol Morris  
• Miss Universe 1960 Linda Bement  
• Miss Universe 1967 Sylvia Hitchcock  
• Miss Universe 1980 Shawn Weatherly  
• Miss Universe 1995 Chelsi Smith  
• Miss Universe 1997 Brooke Lee  
• Miss Universe 2012 Olivia Culpo  
• Miss Universe 2022 R’Bonney Gabriel.
Olivia Culpo is one of the strongest names to come out of the Miss USA pageant in recent history. The 2012 winner is a social media influencer who has partnered with Miu Miu, Estée Lauder and other brands, and stars in “The Culpo Sisters” reality show. She has also demonstrated her acting abilities in “I Feel Pretty” and “Venus as a Boy.”
In the ’60s, a rule was established by the organization which stated that if a Miss USA wins the Miss Universe title, the first runner-up would take over the Miss USA title for the rest of that year.
Diversity in the Miss USA history
Macel Wilson became the first Asian American woman to win Miss USA in 1962, while Miss USA 2022 R’Bonney Gabriel was the first Filipina American to win the pageant and the second Asian American woman to win Miss Universe.
NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - JANUARY 11: Miss USA, R'bonney Gabriel walks onstage during The 71st Miss Universe Competition National Costume Show at New Orleans Morial Convention Center on January 11, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Josh Brasted/Getty Images)
Carole Gist was the first African American woman to wear the Miss USA crown in 1990. Since then, 11 more Black contestants have won the title, including Miss USA 1993 Kenya Moore, who became one of the stars of “Real Housewives of Atlanta” and is the founder of her namesake hair care brand, and Miss USA 2020 Asya Branch, who made headlines for singing the national anthem at one of Donald Trump’s rallies in 2018.
Controversies
In 1957, Mary Leona Gage was disqualified after winning the crown. It was discovered that she had lied about her age, marital status and having children, which led to her being dethroned just a few days after her crowning. Charlotte Sheffield was named Miss USA 1957 and represented the country in the Miss Universe that year.
In 2000, Miss USA 1991 Kelli McCarty left the pageant world to become an adult film star. She later received a nomination as Best Actress for an AVN Award, considered the Oscars of the adult video industry. In 2006, the reigning Miss USA Tara Conner entered a drug rehabilitation program during her reign and later became an advocate against drug addiction.
Age restriction
Previously, the age limit for Miss USA pageant contestants was 18 and 28. In September, it was announced that the pageant would eliminate age limits for delegates over 18 years old starting in 2024.
The youngest Miss USA in history was Myrna Hansen, who was crowned at 17 in 1953. The oldest winner is R’bonney Gabriel, who was 28 when she won.
Since 1983, girls aged 14 to 19 can compete in the Miss Teen USA pageant.
Every winner of the Miss USA through the years
Miss USA 1952: Jackie Loughery
LOS ANGELES - JANUARY 10: The Bob Cummings Show (aka: Love That Bob). A CBS television situation comedy. Episode, Eleven Angry Women. Featuring Jackie Loughery (as Harriet Burke, the Beach Bandit). Originally broadcast January 10, 1957. (Photo by CBS via Getty Images) 
Image Credit: CBS via Getty Images
Jackie Loughery was crowned Miss USA in 1952, representing New York. She was born in Brooklyn in 1930 and began her career as a model and actress before winning the beauty pageant. Loughery went on to become a successful actress, appearing in films such as “The Naked Street,” “Pardners” and “The Hot Angel.”
Miss USA 1953: Myrna Hansen
July 1953:  Full-length portrait of Myrna Hansen, Miss United States of America and second runner-up in the Miss Universe Pageant, holding a trophy while wearing a swimsuit and high heels, Long Beach, California.  (Photo by Hulton Archive/Getty Images) 
Image Credit: Getty Images
Myrna Hansen was crowned Miss USA in 1953, representing Illinois. She was born in 1934 in Chicago and worked as a model before winning the pageant. After her reign as Miss USA, Hansen pursued a career in acting, appearing in films such as “Raintree County,” “Party Girl,” “The Best of Everything” and “Goodbye Charlie.”
Miss USA 1954: Miriam Stevenson
(Original Caption) Christianne Martel, last year's Miss Universe, crowns this year's winner, blonde Miriam Stevenson. A South Carolina coed, Miss Stevenson was elected Miss united States prior to the July 23rd judging of the Miss Universe contest. 
Image Credit: Bettmann Archive
Miriam Stevenson was crowned Miss USA in 1954, representing South Carolina. Stevenson went on to compete in the Miss Universe pageant, where she received a tied final score with Martha Rocha of Brazil. She ended up being crowned the winner due to her physique, becoming the first American to win the competition.
Miss USA 1955: Carlene King Johnson
(Original Caption) Miss U.S.A. Long Beach, California: Statuesque Carlene King Johnson, "Miss Vermont," sits enthroned as Miss United States after her selection at Long Beach, California. The 22 year old jewelry designer, 5'5" tall, was not one of the finalists in the Miss Universe contest. The Rutland, Vermont, beauty won a $200 a week contract with Universal-International Studios, a pearl necklace, a sterling silver compact and a gold trophy. 
Image Credit: Bettmann Archive
Carlene King Johnson was crowned Miss USA in 1955, representing Vermont. She was born in 1933 in Burlington and worked as a model before winning the pageant. She also attended the Forsyth School of Dental Hygiene at Tufts University in Boston.
Miss USA 1956: Carol Morris
LOS ANGELES - OCTOBER 5,1957: Miss Universe 1956 Carol Morris poses for portraits in Los Angeles,CA. (Photo by Earl Leaf/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images) 
Image Credit: Getty Images
Carol Morris was crowned Miss USA in 1956, representing Iowa. After her reign as Miss USA, Morris pursued a career in modeling and acting. She was a regular on game shows like “To Tell the Truth” and “Password”.
Miss USA 1957: Mary Leona Gage (Disqualified)
Mrs. Mary Leona Gage Ennis, the young lady who won the title of Miss U.S.A. in the Miss Universe contest and then lost it when it was discovered she was married and the mother of two children, is shown in this photo made in 1956 with her husband, Gene and their sons David, left, and Gene Jr. at the time she was 17 years old. 
Image Credit: Bettmann Archive
Mary Leona Gage was crowned Miss USA in 1957, representing Maryland. After winning the pageant, it was discovered that she had lied about her age, marital status and having children, which led to her being dethroned just a few days after her crowning. Gage passed away in 2010 at the age of 71.
Miss USA 1957: Charlotte Sheffield
Charlotte Sheffield (Miss USA at international airport), 16 May 1958. (Handout).. (Photo by Los Angeles Examiner/USC Libraries/Corbis via Getty Images) 
Image Credit: Corbis via Getty Images
Charlotte Sheffield was crowned Miss USA in 1957, but it was only for the Miss Universe pageant, following the disqualification of Mary Leona Gage. Sheffield represented Utah.
Miss USA 1958: Arlene Howell
Kino. Das Starlet Arlene Howell, USA, 1950er Jahre. Starlet Arlene Howell, USA, 1950s. (Photo by FilmPublicityArchive/United Archives via Getty Images) 
Image Credit: FilmPublicityArchive/United Arch
Miss USA 1958 Arlene Howell, born Eurlyne Howell, represented Louisiana. She married pilot Paul LaCava in August 1959. She also played “Cindy Lou Brown” in three episodes of “Maverick” and appeared once as a character named “Ladybird Forge.”
Miss Universe 1959: Terry Huntingdon
Girls, 9 July 1961. Lisa Simone ('Miss France');Terry Lynn Huntingdon ('Miss USA of 1960'). (Handout).;Supplementary material reads: ' Caption: Lisa Simon 'Miss France' (light dress). Terry Lynn Huntingdon ('Miss U.S.A.')'.. (Photo by Los Angeles Examiner/USC Libraries/Corbis via Getty Images) 
Image Credit: Corbis via Getty Images
Terry Lynn Huntingdon was born in 1938 in San Francisco and worked as a model before winning the pageant. After her reign as Miss USA, she appeared on “Perry Mason” as defendant Kitty Wynne in “The Case of the Bartered Bikini” and was a contestant on the television quiz show “You Bet Your Life.” Huntingdon.
Miss USA 1960: Linda Bement
(Original Caption) Miami Beach: Linda Bement of Salt Lake City (Utah), the new Miss U. S. A., after her selection from 15 semifinalists in U. S. section of the Miss Universe competition. She is 18, 5'6, 120 lbs., 37-23-36, with green eyes and black hair. She competes with international beauties for the Miss Universe title.
Linda Bement was crowned Miss USA in 1960, representing Utah. She was born in 1940 in Salt Lake City and worked as a model and a secretary before winning the pageant. Bement was a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. In 1962, she married U.S. Racing Hall of Fame Thoroughbred racing jockey Manuel Ycaza.
Miss USA 1961: Sharon Brown
Sharon Brown represented Louisiana. She worked as a model and actress after her reign and passed away in 1985 at the age of 44 due to complications from pneumonia. She became the first Miss USA to win the pageant’s Photogenic Award.
Miss USA 1962: Macel Wilson
Macel Wilson represented Hawaii. She was the first Asian American and first woman of color to win the title. Wilson moved to Denmark and became a film editor for the Danish Broadcasting Corporation (DR).
Miss USA 1963: Marite Ozers
Marite Ozers was born in Latvia and, along with her family, immigrated to Chicago as refugees during World War II.
Miss USA 1964: Bobbi Johnson
June 1965:  Bobbi Johnson, Miss USA 1964, and American actor and singer Pat Boone lean against a pillar in a full-length promotional portrait for the 'Miss USA 1965 Beauty Pageant,' in which Boone and Johnson appeared. Johnson is wearing a crown and a sash over a bathing suit.  (Photo by CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images)
Bobbi Johnson represented the District of Columbia. She worked as an applications engineer in the computer department of General Electric and as a tax accountant.
Miss USA 1965: Sue Downey
(Original Caption) Miss U.S.A. 1965, Sue Ann Downey of Columbus, Ohio (center) with her court, Jane Nelson, Arizona (2nd); Diana Batts, D.C. (5th); Judy Baldwin, New Mexico (3rd); and Julie Andrus, Kentucky (4th), June 4th. The 20-year-old blond will represent the U.S. in the Miss Universe pageant in July.
After winning the Miss Ohio USA title, Downey went on to win the Miss USA 1965 title. She also competed in the 1965 Miss Universe pageant, where she placed as the Second Runner-up and received the Best National Costume award.
Miss USA 1966: Maria Remenyi
(Bettmann Archive/Getty Images)
Maria Remenyi was born in Denmark and migrated to the United States in 1956. She studied astrophysics at the University of California at Berkeley and, in 1971, she hosted the “Maria’s Morning Show” on the radio.
Miss USA 1967 Sylvia Hitchcock
(Original Caption) Newly crowned Miss Universe, Sylvia Hitchcock is seen here with her court on July 15th. They were Jennifer Lewis, England; Mariela Perez Branger, Venezuela; Batva Kabiri, Israel; and Ritva Helena Lehto, Finland.
Sylvia Hitchcock represented Alabama. She won the Miss Universe 1967 and worked for a television station in Miami. Hitchcock died at 69 due to cancer in 2015.
Miss USA 1967: Cheryl Patton
MAR 15 1968, 4/1/1968; Vicki Hissong ; Queen Emerald Isle; Cheryl Ann Patton - Miss USA; 701 N.E. 155 Terrace; N. Hollywood Beach Fl.; Credit:Denver Post  (Photo By Floyd H. McCall/The Denver Post via Getty Images)
In the 1960s, a rule was established by the organization which stated that if a Miss USA wins the Miss Universe title, the first runner-up would take over the Miss USA title for the rest of that year. Following the victory of Carol Morris at the Miss Universe that year, the first runner-up of the competition refused to take over the crown and Cheryl Patton, second runner-up, became Miss USA.
Miss USA 1968: Dorothy Anstett
(Original Caption) A radiant Dorothy Anstett of Kirkland, Washington, poses with her newly won Miss USA trophy. She will enter the Miss Universe contest in July as representative of the United States. Miss USA is one of eight sisters and brothers, is 20 years old, measures 40-25-36 and is 5 ft. 9 in. tall and weighs 127 pounds. She has brown hair and brown eyes.
Dorothy Anstett represented Michigan. She was an English major at the University of Washington and married legendary basketball player Bill Russell in 1977. They later divorced in 1980.
Miss USA 1969: Wendy Dascomb
FEB 18 1970, FEB 19 1970; Miss U.S.A., Wendy Dascomb; Controversial topics off limits.;  (Photo By Steve Larson/The Denver Post via Getty Images)
Wendy Dascomb represented Virginia. She was an activist for women’s rights and studied liberal arts at Stratford College in Danville, Virginia.
Miss USA 1970: Deborah Shelton
CANADA - NOVEMBER 11:  Deborah Shelton   (Photo by Reg Innell/Toronto Star via Getty Images)
Deborah Shelton represented Virginia. In 1974, Shelton posed on the cover of Playboy. She starred in the feature film “Blood Tide” and appeared on multiple television shows, including “Fantasy Island,” “The A-Team” and “T. J. Hooker.”
Miss USA 1971: Michele McDonald
Tanya Wilson, 21, of Honolulu, is crowned Miss U.S.A. of 1972 by Michele McDonald, of Butler, Pennsylvania, Miss U.S.A. of 1971, at conclusion of annual pageant. At right is Bob Barker, master of ceremonies.
Michele McDonald represented Pennsylvania. She had three children with husband Jeffrey Sturgill, with whom she was married for 37 years. In 2018, she went through a double lung transplant at UPMC Presbyterian Hospital in Pittsburgh. McDonald died two years later in a nursing home.
Miss USA 1972: Tanya Wilson
5/20/1972- San Juan, Puerto Rico: Tanya Wilson, Miss U.S.A., of Honolulu, wears crown and is surrounded by runners-up in the pageant.
Tanya Wilson represented Hawaii. Wilson was studying physical education at the University of Hawai and was set to graduate the weekend after Miss USA. She was the second woman from Hawaii to win Miss USA.
Miss USA 1973: Amanda Jones
Bob Barker and Amanda Jones (Miss Illinois) during 1973 Miss USA Pageant at Broadway Theater in New York City, New York, United States. (Photo by Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
Amanda Jones represented Illinois. She was an activist for the feminist movement and openly pro-choice on abortion and against the Vietnam War.
Miss USA 1974: Karen Morrison
(Original Caption) "M USA" of 1974, Karen Jean Morrison, 19, of St. Charles Illinois, relaxes at Hotel Americana during press conference here 5/23. The statuesque 5'11", blue-eyed blonde is a near-perfect 36-25-36.
Karen Morrison represented Illinois. In 1976, she abandoned her model career and embraced fundamentalist Protestant Christianity. She went on to tour the country representing a non-profit organization called Sharing Ministries.
Miss USA 1975: Summer Bartholomew
Miss USA, Summer Bartholomew at the airport.Miss USA, Summer Bartholomew, arrived in Sydney this morning as part of a world tour to; remote the US Bicentennial. March 21, 1976. (Photo by Kevin John Berry/Fairfax Media via Getty Images).
Summer Bartholomew represented California. In the ’80s, she hosted the game show “Sale of the Century” and was briefly part of the “Wheel of Fortune” family. Later, she appeared in the film “Love Is Forever,” with Priscilla Presley.
Miss USA 1976: Barbara Peterson
Beauty queen...Miss USA Barbara Peterson at an interview in the Mandarin Oriental Hotel.Â 26MAR77 (Photo by Sam Chan/South China Morning Post via Getty Images)
 Barbara Peterson represented Minnesota. She became the first Miss USA not to advance to the semifinals in the Miss Universe. Peterson is currently the president of the Burwell Family Foundation.
Miss USA 1977: Kimberly Tomes
LOS ANGELES - JANUARY 1: Miss USA, Kimberly Tomes, and Bob Barker. 1978. (Photo by CBS via Getty Images)
Kimberly Tomes represented Texas. She graduated in physical education from Texas A&M University and later hosted the Miss Texas USA pageant for 12 years.
Miss USA 1978: Judi Andersen
Judi Andersen represented Hawaii. After winning Miss USA, Andersen became an actress and worked on “Fantasy Island”, “Magnum,” “P.I.” and “Jake and the Fatman.”
Miss USA 1979: Mary Therese Friel
Miss Universe entrant, Miss USA, Mary Therese Friel. July 01, 1979. (Photo by Russell McPhedran/Fairfax Media via Getty Images).
Mary Therese Friel represented New York. After winning, Friel signed with Ford Modeling Agency and traveled the world as a model. In 1983, she moved to Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and became a teacher at a local junior college. She is also the founder of s the founder of Mary Therese Friel, LLC, a pageant coaching and image consulting company.
Miss USA 1980: Shawn Weatherly
21st July 1980:  Miss USA, Shawn Weatherly, gives a victory wave after she was crowned 'Miss Universe 1980' at the Seoul Cultural Centre, South Korea.  (Photo by Keystone/Getty Images)
Shawn Weatherly represented South Carolina. After winning Miss USA and Miss Universe in 1980, Weatherly pursued a career in acting. She starred as Jill Riley in “Baywatch” and as Cadet Karen Adams in “Police Academy 3: Back in Training.”
Miss USA 1980: Jineane Ford
Jineane Ford represented Arizona. She was the first runner-up on the Miss USA 1980 and assumed the title after Shawn Weatherly won Miss Universe.
Miss USA 1981: Kim Seelbrede
NEW YORK CITY - OCTOBER 26:   Miss USA 1981 Kim Seelbrede attends the "Red and White" Italian Themed Fashion Show and Cocktail Party on October 26, 1981 at Regine's in New York City. (Photo by Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
Kim Seelbrede represented Ohio. She holds a graduate degree from New York University. After her reign, she founded Kim Seelbrede Coaching, a life coaching and therapy practice.
Miss USA 1982: Terri Utley
Terri Utley represented Arkansas. After her reign, Britt studied journalism and worked as a news anchor on Movietime television, currently known as E!, covering the Academy Awards and the Cannes Film Festival.
Miss USA 1983: Julie Hayek
NEW YORK CITY - SEPTEMBER 15:   Miss USA 1983 Julie Hayek attends the Maybelline-Miss Universe Press Luncheon: Meet Miss Universe 1983 Lorraine Downes, Miss USA 1983 Julie Hayek and Miss Teen USA 1983 Ruth Zakarian on September 15, 1983 at La Cigale in New York City. (Photo by Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
Julie Hayek represented California. Since winning the pageant, she has appeared on the TV series “Dallas,” “Twin Peaks,” “Moonlighting” and others. She has also modeled for Victoria’s Secret, Christian Dior, Warnaco, Natori and Mattel.
Miss USA 1984: Mai Shanley
LOS ANGELES - JANUARY 1: Pictured from left is Miss Universe (1983) Lorraine Downes, of New Zealand and Miss USA (1984) Mai Shanley, of New Mexico. (Photo by CBS via Getty Images)
Mai Shanley represented New Mexico. She was the second Eurasian delegate to win Miss USA.

MANILA, Philippines — The United States remains to be the most successful country in the Miss Universe pageant with eight winners before the most recent edition was held, one titleholder more from close second Venezuela. But with R’Bonney Gabriel’s recent win, the leader moves further away from its staunch rival in the parade of beauties.
Gabriel, whose father is a Filipino man born in Manila, scored the US’ ninth crown at the culmination of the 71st Miss Universe pageant, which is considered its 2022 edition, at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Jan. 14 (Jan. 15 in Manila).
Now with the US having nine total winners, Venezuela has some catching up to do, and so do the other countries with multiple winners, including the Philippines.
The US’ dominance started in 1954 when Miriam Stevenson won in the third Miss Universe pageant held within its borders. Two years later, Carol Morris scored the second victory. In 1960 and 1967, Linda Bement and Sylvia Louise Hitchcock became the third and fourth Misses USA to capture the international title, respectively.
The US waited 13 more years before Shawn Weatherly brought the crown back to the US in 1980, and another 15 years when Chelsi Smith became the sixth Miss USA to be proclaimed as Miss Universe in 1995.
Two years after scoring an historic sixth win, the US captured its seventh crown through Brook Lee in 1997, but waited 15 more years before Olivia Culpo clinched the seventh victory in 2012.
Venezuela’s back-to-back win; Puerto Rico’s five queens
Venezuela started relatively late, with Maritza Sayalero winning its first Miss Universe crown only in 1979. She was followed by Irene Saez in 1981, Barbara Palacios in 1986, and Alicia Machado in 1996.
In 2008 and 2009, the Latin American country recorded the first and only back-to-back victories in the Miss Universe pageant courtesy of Dayana Mendoza and Stefania Fernandez, Venezuela’s fifth and sixth winners. The last Venezuelan contender to capture the title is Gabriela Isler who won in 2013.
Puerto Rico is the third most successful territory in the Miss Universe pageant with five winners—Marisol Malaret in 1970, Deborah Carthy-Deu in 1985, Dayanara Torres in 1993, Denise Quiñones in 2001, and Zuleyka Rivera in 2006.
Philippines, other countries
The Philippines has a total of four Miss Universe titleholders—Gloria Diaz in 1969, Margarita Moran in 1973, Pia Wurtzbach in 2015, and Catriona Gray in 2018.
Sweden, South Africa, Mexico, and India each have three Miss Universe winners and are all tied for being the fifth most successful country in the global tilt. With the exception of the aforementioned European nation, these countries recorded their third victories in the international pageant’s three previous editions.

In this article, we will talk about the world’s most beautiful women who have won the coveted title of the Miss World beauty pageant. The longest-running prestigious Miss World pageant was founded in 1951 by the British businessman Mr. Eric Morely with his wife Madam Julia Morley by his side. The London-based international pageant has managed to crown many successful winners who have gone on to become international celebrities in the film industry, politics, business, media and other fields. We will discuss the Top 10 Most Beautiful Miss World Winners based on their physical beauty, personality, and life after the pageant with the 10th position.
10th Place Miss World 1992 Julia Alexandrovna Kourotchkina — Russia
Julia Alexandrovna Kourotchkina (Russian: Юлия Александровна Курочкина) is a Russian actress, model, and former beauty queen who was crowned Miss Russia 1992 and was later crowned Miss World 1992 in Sun City, South Africa making her the first Russian to be crowned Miss World. She also served as one of the judges for Miss World 2005.
Final Question: How do you answer those critics who regard any beauty pageants as demeaning to women?
She replied: I think Miss World is the contest of the world and this is the contest to help to the whole world. I guess because everybody must love women.
9th Place Miss World 2005 Unnur Birna Vilhjálmsdóttir — Iceland
She was crowned Miss World 2005 on 10 December 2005, in the Beauty Crown Theatre located in the Chinese beach city of Sanya, by the reigning beauty queen, 2004’s Miss Peru Maju Mantilla. She studied anthropology at the University of Iceland and planned to proceed with studies for a lawyer. During the summer of 2005, Unnur Birna did temporary work as a police officer at Keflavík International Airport. She was the chairperson of the college social club and teaches dance. She enjoys acting, singing, all types of dancing, snowboarding, hiking, camping, and horsemanship, and has a special talent for choreography and playing the piano. In 1983, her mother won the Miss Iceland pageant and became a finalist at the Miss World pageant. During the international pageant, her mother was 4 months pregnant which was against the rules of the pageant.
Question asked to was: What has been your favorite moment from the whole contest?
Answer: I have to say the arrival, the people here are amazingly friendly and the scenery is absolutely stunning.
Image 4
8th Place Miss World 1976 Cindy Breakspeare — Jamaica
Breakspeare was born in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, to a Jamaican father, Louis Breakspeare, who was a British-Jamaican of multiracial ancestry, and a white Canadian mother of British origin, Marguerite Cochrane. She has three brothers and one sister. She was invited to participate in the Miss World competition in 1976 held in London and ended up winning the main crown, making her the second Jamaican woman to win the Miss World title.
During the semi-finalist interview, the host asked her: Apart from yourself, what are the famous sites in Jamaica?
She said: The beaches, we have beautiful mountains and some other things of historic interest.
7th Place Miss World 1995 Jacqueline Aguilera — Venezuela
She participated in Top Model of the World 1995, held in Moscow, Russia, where she became Venezuela’s first titleholder in history. Aguilera competed in 1995 as Miss Nueva Esparta in her country’s national beauty pageant, obtaining the title of Miss World Venezuela and the right to represent her country in Miss World 1995. At the Miss World Pageant on 18 November 1995 in Sun City, South Africa, she won the crown as the 45th Miss World, as well as the Photogenic award.
If you could be granted one wish in your life, what would it be and why?
Answer: Her one wish would be for the whole world to continue together to fight for progress and try to improve the world for a better place for the whole of humanity.
Image 5
6th Place Miss World 2004 María Julia Mantilla — Peru
Born in Trujillo, Mantilla is the younger of two daughters of Olmedo Lucio Mantilla Mayer and Elvia Elizabeth García Linares. She was studying to become a high school teacher and planned to start a second degree in Tourism. One of her dreams was to own an online tourism company to promote her native town and country all over the world. Her city, Trujillo, is a mixture of colonial and pre-Columbian architecture. In 2001, Mantilla became the Peruvian national champion of Triathlon and Pentathlon and was elected national athlete of the year. She is a professional dancer in The Marinera, a typical local dance. With a group of ladies, she developed a program in Trujillo to give breakfast to hundreds of children in poor areas. She is a professional dancer. On 4 December 2004, in the Beauty Crown Theatre located in the Chinese beach city of Sanya, she was crowned Miss World 2004 by the winner from the year before, Rosanna Davison of Ireland, becoming the second winner from Peru since Madeline Hartog-Bel in 1967. She has also been crowned Miss World Americas.
Question asked to María: What are you going to miss most about this place when you leave?
She replied: What I am going to miss the most is the people here in Sanya, China. Everyone is very human here because every morning when we wake up, everyone gave us a very nice smile. It is true that I do not speak all the languages but this smile has given us a lot of meaning. Thank you very much, Sanya.
5th Place Miss World 2001 Agbani Darego — Nigeria
Abonnema-native Darego was born in Lagos to a family as the sixth of eight children. As a teenager, Darego longed to be a model, and auditioned for the M-Net Face of Africa modeling competition despite her conservative father’s wishes, but was not chosen as a finalist. Darego attended Federal Government Girls’ College, Abuloma. Upon completing her secondary education she attended the University of Port Harcourt where she studied Computer Science and Mathematics. In 2001, Darego has crowned Most Beautiful Girl in Nigeria. Contrary to popular belief, Darego did not replace Valerie Peterside after the latter was dethroned; Peterside had competed in a rival pageant Miss Nigeria. A few months later she was a contestant in Miss Universe and became the first Nigerian to place among the top 10 semi-finalists, finishing seventh overall. She was the only top ten contestants to wear a modest maillot as opposed to a revealing bikini during the swimsuit competition. In November of that year, she became the first Indigenous African to claim the Miss World title (Past winners Penelope Coelen and Anneline Kriel, both of South Africa, are of European descent, and Antigone Costanda, who represented Egypt in 1954 is of Greek heritage). Darego’s victory was widely welcomed in her home country, and her one-year tenure included goodwill trips and scheduled appearances on behalf of the pageant, and an MFR.
Question: If you are stucked on a desert island and you have to take three thing along what will you take?

1 Bible : because I am a Christian and I know once I have a Bible and read it ,I will be as strong as I can be and with my faith in God, I will definitely survive it.
2 Water : because I need it
3 Blanket to cover myself from cold.
4th Place Miss World 2014 Rolene Strauss — South Africa
At age 15, when she won the Elite Model Look South Africa competition in 2007. Strauss later placed in the top 5 of Miss South Africa 2011, where Melinda Bam became the winner. After 3 years, she returned to Miss South 2014 where she ended up becoming the winner of the biggest national pageant in her country. In December 2014, she competed in the Miss World 2014 contest in London, United Kingdom, and during the final question and answer round, Rolene was asked:
Question: Why should you be the next Miss World? to which Rolene responded:
I believe that the story of my book is more meaningful than my cover. Being proudly South African, I have firsthand experience that unity, respect, and forgiveness exist and those are the aspirations of the Miss World Organization. So, it would be amazing to represent an organization that is a beacon of hope to the world.
She was a medical student at the University of the Free State. She was born in Volksrust, South Africa, to Theresa, a nurse, and Hennie Strauss, a doctor. She is a test tube baby. In her own words “I’m a test tube baby and I believe my passion for health was born with me”. Strauss became engaged to D’Niel Strauss (no relation) in December 2014. They were later married on 6 February 2016, at the Laurent Wedding venue in Somerset West. Their first child, a son, was born in January 2017. In February 2020, she gave birth to her second son. Rolene Strauss is a devout Christian.
3rd Place Miss World 2022 Karolina Bielawska — Poland
Karolina is a Polish model, television presenter, and beauty queen who was crowned Miss World 2021. She became the second titleholder from Poland, the first one being Aneta Kręglicka who won the pageant in 1989. She was born in Łódź, Poland. She is a business student with a bachelor’s degree in management and she is studying for her master’s degree. She is the daughter of Agnieszka Zakrzewska-Bielawska, dean of the Faculty of Organization and Management of the Lodz University of Technology, and Łukasz Bielawski, former president of ŁKS Łódź. In 2022, Karolina joined the 70th Anniversary Miss World beauty pageant in Puerto Rico where she won the coveted title beating 96 delegates.
What is the most important discovery yet to be discovered? was question asked Karolina.
She answered, “Every day we learn something new. We all have unique experiences and all of us can learn something about ourselves. What I’ve discovered is that it costs us so little to enrich the lives of others. This is the cause we can all afford, and believe me, it’s worth its price. If you would like to discover something new, just try to learn to be rich in more empathy, compassion, in gratitude, because we can all do what, as I mentioned before. We can all be great because everyone can serve. And this discovery feels like so simple, but it’s actually [life-willing].”
Her classic and elegant blond hair and blue eyes beauty resembles Hollywood actress Margot Robbie has made Karolina one of the most be-loved Miss World winners due to her kind heart and down to earth personality.
2nd Place Miss World 2013 Megan Young — Philippines
Megan was born on February 27, 1990, in Alexandria, Virginia to Victoria Talde, from Pandan, Antique, and American Calvin Cole Young III. She studied filmmaking at De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde. She has worked as an actress with GMA Artist Center and ABS-CBN. In 2013, she joined the Miss World beauty pageant which was held in Bali, Indonesia where she became the first Filipina woman to win the blue Miss World crown. Her youthful and charismatic personality made her a fan favorite among many international pageant fans. She also bagged the Best in Fashion Runway, Miss Sports by Fila, Miss Reducin, Miss Olay, Miss Laguna, Miss Figlia, and Miss Bench Body awards.
Final Question: Why should you be Miss World?
Megan Young Answer — The Miss World for me treasures the core values of humanity. Core values guide people on the way they act and the way they do. I will use this to show other people how they can understand each other. As one, we can help society.
In February 2017, Mikael Daez confirmed that he had been dating Young for six years, and the revelation was made after so long due to work commitments. On January 25, 2020, they announced their marriage.
The Most Beautiful Miss World winner is Miss World 1994 Aishwarya Rai — India
Aishwarya Rai Bachchan (Hindi: ऐश्वर्या राय बच्चन) is an Indian actress who is primarily known for her work in Hindi and Tamil films. In 1994, Aishwarya joined the Femina Miss India 1994 beauty pageant where she was the fan favorite for the national pageant title where she became 1st Runner Up to Sushmita Sen who went on to win Miss Universe 1994. In November 1994, Aishwarya competed in the 44th edition of the Miss World pageant, which was held on 19 November 1994 and marked the third consecutive staging of Miss World in Sun City, South Africa. Her remarkable beauty, dazzling style, and contagious personality made her win the second Miss World crown for her country — India.
Final Question: What qualities should Miss World 1994 embody?
She said, The Miss Worlds that we have had up to date, have been proof enough that they have had compassion. Compassion for the underprivileged and not only for the people who have status and stature.
She has established herself as one of the most popular celebrities in India. Rai has received numerous accolades, including two Filmfare Awards, and was honored with the Padma Shri by the Government of India in 2009 and the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres by the Government of France in 2012. She has often been cited in the media as “the most beautiful woman in the world”. Many years of humanitarian work that she has contributed to underprivileged people was recognized with Lifetime Beauty with a Purpose Award during Miss World 2014 in London, United Kingdom.
